senses.gloss:
घण् घण्, cl. 8. P. A. घणोति, -णुते, &c.,
to shine; (a various reading for घृण्.)

घण्ट् घण्ट्, cl. 1. P. and 10. P. घण्टति
and घण्टयति, &c., to speak; shine.

घण्ट घण्ट, अस्, m. (said to be fr. rt. हन्,
perhaps related to घट above), a N. of Śiva [cf.
अ-घण्ट, धटिन् or घटिन् (?), घण्टिन्, and
चण्डिक-घण्ट], a kind of dish [cf. मत्स्य-
घण्ट]; a sort of sauce, vegetables made into a
pulp and mixed with turmeric and mustard seeds and
capsicums; (आ), f. a bell; also a plate of iron or mixed
metal struck as a clock, (a form घण्टी occurs in
क्षुद्र-घण्टी, a small bell); N. of several plants,
= घण्टा-पाटलि; another plant, Sida Cordifolia
and Rhombifolia; also Uraria Lagopodioides; also
Achyranthes Aspera [cf. अपामार्ग]; (ई), f. a N. of
Durgā, as having a clear voice (?).
—घण्ट-फ-
लक, अस् or अम् (?), m. or n. (?), a shield with a
ringing sound, or a shield furnished with small bells.
(घण्ट = घण्टा ?).
—घण्टा-कर्ण, अस्, m.
one who has ears as broad as a bell, or whose ears
are decorated with bells; N. of an attendant of
Skanda; also one of Śiva's attendants, who is sup-
posed to preside over cutaneous complaints, and is
worshipped for exemption from them in the month
Caitra; N. of a Piśāca attendant on Kuvera.
—घण्टागार (˚टा-आग्˚), अम्, n. a belfry.
—घण्टा-ताड, अस्, m. a bell-man, one who strikes
a bell or Gharī.
—घण्टा-ताडन, अम्, n. striking
a bell.
—घण्टा-नाद, अस्, m. the sound of a bell
&c.
—घण्टा-पथ, अस्, m. the chief road through
a village, a highway, (i. e. the bell-road, or that by
which elephants &c., decorated with tinkling orna-
ments, proceed); N. of Mallinātha's commentary on
the Kirātārjunīya.
—घण्टा-पाटलि, इस्, m., N. of a
plant, commonly called Ghaṇṭāpārali, a species of the
trumpet-flower with bell-shaped blossoms, Bignonia
Suaveolens.
—घण्टाभ (˚टा-आभा), अस्, m., N. of
a Daitya; (a various reading for घटाभ, q. v.)
—घण्टा-रव, अस्, m. the sound of a bell; (आ), f.
Crotolaria of various species.
—घण्टाली (˚टा-आली),
f., N. of several cucurbitaceous plants; [cf. कोशातकी.]
—घण्टा-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, furnished with a bell or
with bells.
—घण्टा-वाद्य, अम्, n. the sound of
a clock.
—घण्टा-वीज, अम्, n. the tree Croton
[]
Jamalgota, commonly Jamālgoṭā; the nut of this
tree.
—घण्टा-शब्द, अस्, m. bell-metal, brass;
the sound of a bell.
—घण्टा-स्वन, अस्, m. the
sound of a bell or clock.
—घण्टेश्वर (˚टा-ईश्˚),
अस्, m., N. of a son of Maṅgala (Mars) and Medhā.
—घण्टोदर (˚ट-उद्˚), अस्, m., N. of an attend-
ant of Varuṇa &c.; (a various reading for घटो-
दर, q. v.)

घण्ट; probably for हन्त्र as दण्ड for
दन्त्र.

घण्टक or घण्टाक, अस्, m., N. of a plant,
= घण्टा-पाटलि.

घण्टिका, f. a small bell [cf. क्षुद्र-घण्टिका];
the uvula or soft palate.

घाण्टिक, अस्, m. a bell-ringer, a strolling ballad-
singer who carries a bell; a bard who sings in chorus,
and especially in honour of the gods, ringing a bell
in presence of their images; the plant Datura
Fastuosa.

घण्टिन्, ई, इनी, इ, furnished with bells, sounding
like a bell; an epithet of Śiva; [cf. घण्ट.]
—घण्टिनी-वीज, अम्, n. the tree Croton Jamalgota;
[cf. घण्टा-वीज.]

घण्टु, उस्, m. a string of bells tied on an ele-
phant's chest &c. by way of ornament; heat, light,
&c.; [cf. निघण्टु.]
घण्ड घण्ड, अस्, m. a bee; [cf. घुण्ड.]
